lens: Retro-futurist terminal / switchboard operator: monospace, phosphor glow, call-center nostalgia meets AI
name: Switchboard Console
one_liner: A dark phosphor call console with a patch-panel persona library, a live coach ticker and a paper-white debrief, built on shadcn/ui (Base UI) and IBM Plex.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the switchboard lens: monospace labels, phosphor glow reserved for live signal, patch-cord and jack metaphors for talk-track and persona selection, and an oscilloscope in place of the blurry orb. Changed three things. Glow is limited to the live stage, because full-screen CRT styling hurts AA contrast and long reading. Debrief, library and dashboard stay light "paper" for scanning and printing. The component layer is shadcn/ui on Base UI rather than hand-built Tailwind, because contributors need a standard vocabulary. Research supported this: ElevenLabs, Hume and PlayAI all center a dark voice stage with a transcript panel beside it, so the lens fits the category. Mobbin scorecards (15Five, Uxcel, Charma) are light, so the debrief follows that convention.

ui_stack.name: shadcn/ui on Base UI
ui_stack.why: Copied source lives in the repo, so contributors edit components directly. Base UI is reported as shadcn's default since July 2026 by two third-party write-ups; verify on ui.shadcn.com before committing. Mantine was rejected: it ships its own CSS Modules and no Tailwind, and benchmarks at 163 KB gzip versus 127-154 KB for shadcn variants.

ui_stack.name: Tailwind CSS v4 with CSS variables
ui_stack.role: Token layer for console, paper and print themes
ui_stack.why: One-time migration from v3. Tokens on :root let the same component render dark console and light paper modes.

ui_stack.name: IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono (Google Fonts, OFL)
ui_stack.why: Mono carries timers, scores, transcript timestamps and persona IDs with a terminal heritage; Sans carries body. Replaces Inter and Sora.

ui_stack.name: lucide-react
ui_stack.why: Already in the stack. Used at 1.5px stroke, with custom LED and jack glyphs.

ui_stack.name: Motion
ui_stack.role: Choreography for the cue ticker, patch-cord draw and sheets
ui_stack.why: Limited to a few signature moments; every animation collapses to a fade under prefers-reduced-motion.

ui_stack.name: Canvas 2D oscilloscope
ui_stack.role: Replaces the blurry orb as the voice signal
ui_stack.why: Shows real audio level, reads as signal, and costs far less than three.js on the live screen. Keep three.js only for the landing hero if wanted.

ui_stack.name: cmdk
ui_stack.role: Command palette for library search and quick actions
ui_stack.why: Keyboard-first search across personas, scenarios and calls, fitting the switchboard metaphor.

palette.use: Dark mode app shell and live stage background
Cards and panels on the console
Live signal only: REC dot, LED meters, oscilloscope trace, score fills during a call
Coach cues and unverified live estimates; never on the same element as phosphor
End and grade, and live mic state only
Light mode background for debrief, library, dashboard and print
Body text on paper; dark-mode body text is #E7F3EC
Primary buttons and links on paper (about 6.4:1 on paper for AA)

design_language.typography: IBM Plex Mono 500, 12px uppercase with 0.08em tracking, for labels; Plex Mono with tabular numerals for timers and scores. IBM Plex Sans 400 for body and 600 for headings, display at 40-56px with tight tracking. Glow (text-shadow of about 8px at 40% opacity) only on live numbers.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 4px radius for panels, full-round for jacks and LEDs. 1px hairlines instead of drop shadows, with one elevation step for modals. Jack motif: small circular ports mark talk-track steps and persona status. Scanlines at 3% opacity on the live stage only, off under reduced motion.
design_language.motion: 180ms warm-up flicker when entering a live call. Oscilloscope runs at 60fps only while audio is live. Whisper cue slides in over 200ms with a phosphor fade. Patch-cord SVG draws on persona select. Reduced motion turns all of this into fades.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.5px stroke plus custom LED and jack glyphs. No emoji. Every status pairs color with a text label, so color is never the only signal.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark console is the default (prefers-color-scheme: dark), with a light paper mode on debrief, library and dashboard, and a per-page toggle. Printing always uses paper. Target WCAG AA on every token pair in both modes.

navigation_and_ia: Top bar: Board (library), Patch (pre-call), Log (progress), Team (role-gated), plus a search that opens the command palette. The flow runs Board to Patch to Call to Ticket to Log, and each step carries its next action forward; for example, the weakest criterion on Log pre-selects a Board filter. Routes: /board, /board/new (wizard), /patch/[id], /call/[id], /ticket/[id], /log, /team. On mobile, a bottom tab bar holds Board, Log and a centered Patch button, and Call and Ticket hide it. Demo mode and the no-login path stay. A "Model switchboard" tray names the OpenAI model behind each job, in the footer on desktop and in Settings on mobile.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Coach runs as a separate model call, never as the persona. After each rep turn, a small structured-output call (gpt-4.1-mini, the current default) returns at most one cue as JSON: cue_type, text, rubric_ids and confidence. Target latency is under 2 seconds. Cue types are OBJECTION, NEXT QUESTION, TALK-TRACK STEP and TIME. Rate limit: one cue per 20 seconds, and nothing when confidence is low. Live scoring moves the five rubric LEDs from evidence quotes only. Each LED shows its evidence on hover and is labeled unverified until the post-call grader replaces it. The debrief reuses the same evidence objects, so the live cue, the live LED and the final quote share one trail. Silent mode turns off cues but keeps scoring. Mobile uses the same schema.
persona_library_and_wizard: Library: 300+ seeded personas across 30+ jobs at launch, covering SDR cold call, AE discovery, CS renewal, collections, recruiting, insurance, mortgage, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, procurement and retail. Each persona is one JSON file in /personas with role, industry, difficulty, objection tags, rubric template and opening line, so contributors add personas through a pull request. Wizard: intake from a job description, product URL, CRM note, ICP or pasted transcript. A structured-output call returns a schema-validated persona, a rubric whose weights sum to 100, and a 2-minute test call before anything is saved. 'Export as PR' writes the file and suggests a branch name. Built-ins are read-only; community and mine personas can be duplicated and edited.
signature_moments: Whisper ticker: an amber cue lands in the coach column within two seconds of the rep's last line.
Talk-track jacks: six jacks light on the patch panel as each step is hit, with a short phosphor pulse.
Patch-in: pressing Patch in draws a phosphor cord from the persona card to the console before the call starts.
Call timeline on the ticket: score changes appear as markers on a waveform; clicking one plays that moment.
Shared evidence trail: the live cue, the live LED and the final quote are the same object, so the coach's advice and the grade cannot drift apart.
openai_fund_angle: Show the models, not just a logo. The Model switchboard tray names the OpenAI model behind each job (gpt-realtime-1.5 for voice, which appears in the OpenAI Platform audio UI on Mobbin; gpt-4.1-mini for coaching, grading and the wizard) and shows live cost per call in mono. A fund reviewer can see efficient API use directly. Contributor invitation: the wizard's Export as PR flow, a 'good first persona' label set, and a README section on using Codex to add personas, scenarios and rubric tests. For Codex for Open Source: PR templates and CI that run Codex review on persona-schema changes. The README hero GIF shows a real coach cue with the model named beside it. Show model names as plain facts; do not imply endorsement by OpenAI.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1 (M, 1-2 weeks): move Tailwind 3 to 4, run shadcn init on Base UI, add tokens and Plex fonts, and rebuild the shell, nav and landing. Phase 2 (L): define the persona JSON schema, seed 300 personas in /personas, and build the Board, Patch and wizard. Phase 3 (L): build the coach channel and live cockpit behind a feature flag, keeping the current debrief until parity. Phase 4 (M): Log, Team and the mobile dock. Keep old routes live until each new screen passes existing tests.

risks: Self-scores for judges (my estimates, not a verdict): A 7, B 7, C 8, D 6, E 7, F1 4 (crowded SaaS market: Second Nature, Hyperbound, Yoodli, Gong AI Trainer, Outdoo), F2 6 (BPOs and training firms need SSO, SCORM/LTI and audit trails), F3 3 (worth building as open source, especially for the fund).
Coach latency and cue fatigue: a second model call per turn adds 1-2 seconds and cost. Cap cues, expose Silent mode, and measure p95 latency before shipping the cockpit.
Glow and scanlines can hurt legibility and read as a gimmick. Keep glow off body text, and run AA checks in both themes.
Persona library quality is a content problem. Three hundred seeded personas that are thin or unreviewed would make the library look padded; each needs a rubric test.
Two themes double QA. Build all new components from tokens so each screen inherits both modes.
The shadcn Base UI default and Radix's maintenance status come from third-party write-ups and should be verified on ui.shadcn.com before committing.
Research was 4 Mobbin searches and 2 web searches, so some competitor claims come from vendor blogs and are labeled as such.
